A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AfriqueLLM study. The main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CPT experiments, data-mixture and hyperparameter ablations, multilingual benchmark results, and document-level translation evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Qwen 3/3.5 4B evaluations and an increased code/math-budget ablation.

M1.justification: The CPT procedure, UniMax sampling, data-processing components, and primary CMS recipe remain unchanged. The added backbones and ExtendedCM condition vary experimental configurations and training budgets without introducing a new algorithmic component or inference procedure.

E1.justification: The training sources, 20 African training languages, four high-resource languages, seven AfroBench-Lite tasks, and AFRIDOC-MT scenario are retained. Appendix C lists identical benchmark-language coverage. ExtendedCM increases existing data quantities; expansion beyond 50 African languages is only future work.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen 3 4B and Qwen 3.5 4B as evaluated base comparators. Appendix D removes Lugha-Llama-8B-wura rows from detailed translation, Injongo, and SIB-200 comparisons, and Gemma 3 27B rows from chrF++ comparisons. Both removed comparators remain in the main Table 3 comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 introduces Qwen 3/3.5 4B experimental configurations and ExtendedCM, replacing approximately 1B code plus 1B math tokens with 5B plus 5B. Existing evaluation metrics, prompting settings, and training configurations are retained. The PDFs do not document a protocol change explaining the revised SSA-COMET scores.

E4.justification: New Section 5.5 and Table 7 investigate two central questions: differences between Qwen 3 and Qwen 3.5 at 4B, and whether substantially more code/math data changes their task trade-offs. This adds a substantive analytical branch beyond v1's source-mixture, hyperparameter, and language-transfer analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new appendix average columns summarize performance across languages and do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive 4B results: Table 7 reports adapted overall scores of 54.94, 57.12, and 58.26 for Qwen 3, Qwen 3.5, and ExtendedCM. Existing SSA-COMET results are broadly revised; AfriqueQwen-14B's Table 3 Flores score changes from 65.26 to 63.77 and overall from 63.79 to 63.58. Matched chrF++ and other retained per-language scores remain unchanged. These are reported numerical revisions, without evidence establishing model regressions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. No mathematical definition, assumption, or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and four headline findings retain their meaning: data composition drives CPT gains, architecture matters across model families, base multilingual proficiency does not reliably predict adaptation outcomes, and CPT supports document-level translation. Additional model evaluations and updated summary scores do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 adds a task-dependent interpretation of multilingual priors and increased code/math data, while footnote 7 acknowledges that broader African-language coverage is hypothesized. Section 5.1 narrows monolingual reasoning degradation to Gemma 12B, replacing v1's unsupported 4B example. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that all token counts use the Gemma 3 tokenizer and explicitly identifies Table 3's CPT-language aggregation scope. Appendix prompts, YAML configuration, hardware, and efficiency details are retained. Both versions already announce released models and provide the same collection link; revised release wording does not establish newly available access.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography retain the same works and research positioning. The new Qwen experiments do not introduce a revised novelty claim or additional cited literature.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.5, locally revises Sections 5.1–5.2, updates future-work and release wording, and corrects terminology such as the ambiguous monolingual 'M' label. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 7, expands Table 3 and appendix tables with model rows and average columns, and splits v1's two-direction chrF++ Table 20 into Tables 21–22. Some tables and takeaway boxes move with text reflow. Figure 1 and the overall visual format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence about 4B model selection and code/math budgets, corrects prose that contradicted tables in Sections 5.1–5.2, and clarifies token counting. These improve empirical support and reporting accuracy. The benefit is tempered by unexplained SSA-COMET score revisions and removal of detailed comparator results, which reduce transparency in parts of the evaluation.
